subject: Inter-region hop misroute causing P95/P99 RTT spike - SableHealth escalation
messages:
From: ops@sablehealth.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ctaylor@sablehealth.com
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 08:13:00 -0700
Subject: High latency spike this morning - p95/p99 up 5x

Hi Marissa —

We started seeing a big jump in latency around 07:55 PDT. Our p95 for text-generation calls jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s and p99 is >2.3s. Error rate also spiked briefly. This started at ~07:55 and lasted ~20m, then recurred at 08:40 for a few minutes. Our product team is blocked on a production demo.

Attached are client-side traces and a CSV of request latencies by minute. Please treat as urgent.

Thanks,
Chandra Taylor
Sr. Platform Engineer, SableHealth
ops@sablehealth.com

Chandra —

Sorry you're seeing this. We're looking immediately. I've looped in Jonas (routing) and Dylan (runtime). Can you confirm whether the affected requests were to the hosted text-generation endpoint in us-west-2 and whether any region override headers were set? Also keeping an eye on rate/traffic.

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Cc: ops@sablehealth.com
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency spike this morning - p95/p99 up 5x

Marissa / team —

Initial look at routing logs: between 07:50–08:10 we saw a surge of requests from SableHealth's customer token group being routed to our eu-west-1 POP instead of the expected us-west-2. The edge routing config for regional fallbacks shows a stale route entry pointing that token group to a legacy egress in EU. That explains the +~120–150ms RTT and the p95 jump.

I also see a short-lived routing controller restart around 07:48 (deploy churn on a config push) that likely re-applied the old fallback mapping. No evidence of model runtime degradation — token-level timing on the compute nodes stayed steady.

Action items I'm starting:
- Roll back the fallback map to the canonical version for token group 'sable-prod' (in progress)
- Invalidate edge cache and force repush of routing table to affected POPs
- Gather sample request traces and correlate with compute latency (Jonas -> attaching trace-flows)

I'll post next update when rollback completes.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Network Reliability Engineer
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@sablehealth.com
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency spike this morning - P95/P99 RTT surge

Update — rollback complete at 08:59 PDT. Routing table shows token group 'sable-prod' correctly mapped to us-west-2. Edge propagation logs show all POPs received updated mapping by 09:00.

Post-rollback metrics: p95 for SableHealth dropped back to ~240ms within two minutes, p99 to ~320ms. Error rate returned to baseline. Attaching a short ZIP of screenshots from our dashboards.

Next steps I recommend:
- Full postmortem to be produced (owner: Hannah)
- Short-term credit offer for customer downtime window (Marissa to coordinate commercial)
- Harden routing controller deploys to prevent re-applying legacy maps (Rishi to triage)

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
SRE, Serving Runtime
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai

Attachments: sable_incident_screenshots.zip

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@sablehealth.com
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency spike this morning - postmortem and next steps

Thanks for the quick triage. I'm taking the postmortem. Preliminary timeline:
- 07:47: config push (routing-controller v2.3.1) triggered during routine deploy window
- 07:48: routing-controller restarted and re-applied a legacy fallback map for token groups which included 'sable-prod'
- 07:50–08:12: increased p95/p99 observed as traffic was misrouted to eu-west-1 POPs
- 08:59: rollback completed; propagation finished by 09:00

Root cause hypothesis: a deployment artifact in the routing-controller omitted the canonical fallback map merge step when a feature flag was enabled. Rishi, can you confirm whether the merge logic had an exception at v2.3.1?

Immediate mitigations I'll include in the postmortem:
- Block feature-flagged routing-controller rollouts during high-traffic windows for paid-hosted tenants
- Add monitoring alert if token-group-to-pop mapping changes for specific enterprise tokens
- Test harness to snapshot and validate fallback map merge on staging before rollouts

I'll circulate a draft postmortem by EOD.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Reliability
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ctaylor@sablehealth.com, ops@sablehealth.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency spike this morning - resolution and commercial offer

Chandra / team —

Thanks again for flagging this and for patience while we fixed it. Summary: the latency spike was caused by an erroneous fallback mapping applied during a routing-controller deploy which routed some of your traffic through eu-west-1. We rolled back the mapping and propagation finished by 09:00 PDT; p95/p99 returned to normal.

Commercial next steps: we're prepared to issue a credit for the impacted window (07:48–09:00 PDT). I'll coordinate with Laura on the exact credit calculation — Laura, can you pull your billing view for RD-2345 and propose a credit amount?

Operational next steps: Hannah will circulate a postmortem and Rishi will lead a small engineering fix to prevent the merge omission. We'll also add a monitoring alert for token-group mapping changes.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute readout early next week with our reliability and networking leads.

Apologies again — we're treating this with executive priority.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Hosted API
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
